Risks:
  - Over-broad EXCUSE_PATTERNS could false-positive on legitimate markers that merely mention a dependency; mitigate by requiring Check B recovery (imperative work item) rather than bare phrase bans.
  - Rewriting source markers requires stable line targeting (like remove-stub.js); implement as an atomic whole-file rewrite after validation to avoid read/write races.
Caveats:
  - The operational scope is tools/conver/.claude; crates/siprs/.claude is out of scope for this ticket.
  - MUST RESOLVE markers with no key are legal transiently (insert-stub) but fail Check C at inspection/merge boundaries.

  - Whether the excuse lexicon belongs in a shared module consumed by both validator and preflight.
Future improvements:
  - Extend Check B with a whitelist of accepted imperative verbs from the repository glossary.

tickets.title: resolve-ticket: No-External-Excuse enforcement & integer step renumbering
tickets.background:
The resolve-ticket command is the implementation and resolution phase: the AI resolves warnings, stubs, and crimes here. It currently has three escape points that let the AI be lazy: (1) Step 5 allows deferral for vague reasons without forcing an AI-executable work item; (2) the Step 7.5 escape hatch explicitly lists blocked on external dependency and awaiting another team as valid reasons to defer, which is exactly the terminal excuse the project forbids; (3) the convergence loop checks stub and crime counts but never detects excuse-language markers. This ticket integrates the mechanisms built in PX-120 (preflight-stub-cleanup.js for the resolved-stub sweep, validate-no-external-excuses.js for excuse detection) into resolve-ticket.md as hard gates, renumbers all steps as integers (no decimals, no Step 7.5), and adds creation-time excuse rejection to insert-stub.js so a lazy marker can never be written. The resolve command must never abort: excuse detection enters a validate-fix-revalidate loop until zero excuses remain.

### Goal
Make resolve-ticket converge: after this ticket, every resolve run removes resolved-but-stale markers (Step 4), refuses lazy deferrals (Step 6), and completes only when stub count, crime count, and excuse count are all zero. No terminal-excuse marker can be created or survive a resolve run.

### Purpose
The resolve phase is where the AI has the strongest temptation to defer rather than implement. The purpose is to make deferral structurally impossible without an AI-executable work item and an active ticket key, and to give the executing AI concrete, self-contained instructions (stdout/stderr) for every required action.

### Motivation
The pipeline already diverged twice on the siprs crate (63 stubs referencing past tickets). The same lazy pattern appears in resolve: the escape-hatch text itself teaches the AI that blocked on external dependency is an acceptable reason to stop. The user mandated an absolute rule: no external, no approval-shirking; every blocker is internal AI work.

### Constraints
- Generic, not siprs-specific: applies to any directory plus any Tickets.json.
- The resolve command must never abort; it loops validate-fix-revalidate until green.
- All step numbers are integers (1-10); decimal steps are forbidden.
- The Prohibition (no ticket status changes in Tickets.json) is preserved; deferral uses /make-ticket.
- New stdout/stderr messages must be English, self-contained, and Action-directive.
- TDD: all new script changes follow Red-Green-Refactor with contract coverage C001-C004.

tickets.title: Shared function createTicketFromSource for dedicated ticket-creation scripts
tickets.background:
Goal: Provide the shared core used by create-resolving-ticket.js (find) and create-deferral-ticket.js (resolve) to create a quality NEW ticket from a source ticket's deep clone.
Purpose: A new ticket must inherit the source ticket's structural/relational identity (nodeIds, relatedTicketIds, referenceSection, referenceUrls, sourcePaths, rfcDiscrepancies) with ZERO loss, while its content fields are reset so the AI can rewrite them to the NEW work item — never a retry of the past ticket.
Motivation: add-omission-ticket.js already deep-clones (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) in appendTicket, line 121) and targets the max real phase (lines 113-114), but it writes to _tmp-omissions-*.json, not directly to Tickets.json. find Step 1 and resolve deferral need direct Tickets.json creation (immediate known key for marker rewrite + Check C), non-PX max phase. A shared function avoids duplicating the clone/edit/append/validate logic across two entry scripts.
Constraints: (1) Must never lose relational fields (PRESERVE set: nodeIds, relatedTicketIds, referenceSection, referenceUrls, sourcePaths, rfcDiscrepancies). (2) New ticket must be non-PX max real phase, status='todo'. (3) Must validate via validate-tickets.js before writing (atomic, no partial write). (4) Must return the actual new key. (5) Must strip completed-ticket residue (startedAt/completedAt/round status).

- Internal state invariant: new ticket has status='todo', no completedAt/startedAt, no round-aware status
- Boundary invariant: append targets the max real phase (id=N); never the PX phase (id=-1); creates phase 0 when no non-PX phase exists

tickets.title: Abolish phasify --src-dir: always rewrite source markers in CWD
tickets.background:
Goal: phasify-omissions.js must always rewrite source marker lines to the phasify-duplicate ticket keys after a merge, so the find end-to-end flow (markers → active duplicates) works.
Purpose: The --src-dir flag is never passed by find-omissions.md Step 9 (phasify-omissions.js --graph=$ARGUMENTS), so rewriteSourceMarkerLines (which requires srcDir) never runs — source markers keep referencing the original Step-1 resolving tickets, which phasify freezes as R<round>. Check C then fails on the next gate run.
Motivation: phasify always runs from the Tickets.json directory (CWD), and source markers are always under CWD. The flag has no real use case in the pipeline. Abolishing it and using process.cwd() removes the wiring gap without adding a parameter to the Step 9 command.

tickets.title: consolidate-stubs.md: consolidate the Step 5 blocking gate into a single shell script + trim noise descriptions
tickets.background:
【Goal】Replace the multi-command Step 5 gate with one consolidate-stubs-gate.sh invocation and trim the accompanying explanation to operator-level meaning
【Purpose】The gate is currently 3 commands plus a fragile MANIFEST=$(ls -t ...) subshell that must be copy-pasted, and the explanation walks through each internal script (--for-consolidate / --no-write), which is noise to anyone treating the gate as a black box
【Motivation】Single-script encapsulation makes the gate repeatable, less error-prone, and testable; the description should say what the gate does (what blocks it), not how it is wired
【Constraints】The gate must run from the Tickets.json root; it exits non-zero on any real problem and passes for completed-key re-pointed markers; the Step 5 recovery sequence stays
scope: Path: .claude/scripts/tickets/consolidate-stubs-gate.sh
Action: new shell script — the blocking three-part gate for /consolidate-stubs Step 5

Detail: runs validate-no-external-excuses.js --for-consolidate, validate-stub-format.js --scan ., picks the newest manifests/CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json via 'ls -t | head -1' and pipes it to batch-create-resolving-tickets.js --no-write; set -euo pipefail so any failure aborts with a non-zero exit
Before/After: 3 manual commands + a MANIFEST subshell that must be copy-pasted -> a single 'node .claude/scripts/tickets/consolidate-stubs-gate.sh' invocation
API: node .claude/scripts/tickets/consolidate-stubs-gate.sh — exit 0 when all gates pass, non-zero when blocked; run from the directory containing Tickets.json
Schema: no Tickets.json change
Config: no new configuration
Dep: no new dependencies (reuses the three existing validators)
Non-change item: the three gate commands and their individual semantics; the Step 5 recovery sequence in consolidate-stubs.md
Non-change why: the gate is a composition — the validators stay single-purpose and individually tested
Impact component: /consolidate-stubs Step 5 — a single, repeatable, testable blocking gate
Impact nature: operator reliability — one command instead of a fragile copy-paste sequence
Impact response: consolidate-stubs-gate.sh added; consolidate-stubs.md Step 5 rewritten to one invocation + operator-level description; a gate test added
testUnit:
UT: [C004] the Step 5 description is operator-level — it names what the gate fails on, not how it is wired

testIntegration: IT: a fixture workspace -> run the gate -> exit 0; introduce a malformed marker -> the gate exits 1 (end-to-end gate behavior)
IT: consolidate-stubs.md Step 5 and the gate script agree — the documented command is the script's actual path and runs from the Tickets.json root
IT: existing suites stay green — validate-no-external-excuses, validate-stub-format, batch-create-resolving-tickets are unchanged and individually tested
testExceptions: Item: verifying a deep subprocess failure inside batch-create-resolving-tickets.js --no-write (e.g. Tickets.json corruption mid-gate) — Reason: the manifest is a transient artifact and the validators are individually unit-tested; the gate only orchestrates them with set -euo pipefail, and the deep failure mode cannot test mechanically as a unit assertion because it requires corrupting shared state mid-run. This is not a design defect — the abort path is asserted by the malformed-marker and missing-manifest tests — Alternative: those abort-path tests cover the non-zero propagation; deeper subprocess failure modes are out of scope.

Item: whether the shell orchestration layer can test the node validators' runtime behavior — Reason: the .sh only composes node scripts and cannot test node runtime semantics itself; the validators have their own suites. This is not a design defect — the gate test asserts the orchestration (exit codes), and each validator is covered by its own test file — Alternative: tests/consolidate-stubs-gate.test.cjs asserts the gate's exit behavior; the validators' suites cover their internals.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: a valid fixture tree -> node .claude/scripts/tickets/consolidate-stubs-gate.sh exits 0; consolidate-stubs.md Step 5 shows one command
Error case: a malformed marker or a missing manifest -> the gate exits non-zero
Edge case: multiple CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST files -> the newest is validated; the Step 5 description contains no internal script/flag references

tickets.background:

tickets.title: Make /consolidate-stubs a hard prerequisite of /find-omissions (manifest gate + Step 1 simplification + full-success artifact cleanup)
tickets.background:
- **Goal**: Make /consolidate-stubs a hard, mechanically-enforced prerequisite of /find-omissions. After this ticket, /find-omissions cannot run (its pre-flight exits 2) until a complete consolidated unit manifest exists under ./manifests/, Step 1 is a two-command manifest-driven flow instead of a 4-class manual classification, and a successful full run deletes the transient manifest + rollback artifacts.
- **Purpose**: Guarantee, via the pre-flight gate, that the pipeline consumes exactly what /consolidate-stubs produces. The consolidate Step 5 gate (consolidate-stubs-gate.sh) already proves: no orphan keys, no terminal-excuse plans, all markers re-pointed to valid keys, and a complete grouped unit manifest emitted. Once that guarantee is mandatory, find-omissions Step 1 no longer needs to re-derive it by hand — it just pipes the manifest into batch-create-resolving-tickets.js. This closes the loop so the two commands form one seamless pipeline (the handoff described in WORK-INSTRUCTION-CONSOLIDATE-FIND-OMISSIONS.md §5).
- **Motivation**: The current find-omissions.md Step 1 (L103-151) is a large self-healing gate: it classifies every marker into 4 classes (resolvedCandidates / pendingObligations / orphans / excuses) and gives elaborate manual manifest-authoring guidance. That logic duplicates guarantees the consolidation already enforces, so it is dead weight once consolidation is mandatory. Transient artifacts (CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json, ROLLBACK-*.json) currently accumulate in manifests/ indefinitely — nothing removes them, and the `ls -t | head -1` selector grows fragile as they pile up.
- **Constraints**: TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory (Supreme Law §1); every new script must be dedicated, testable, and default side-effect-free; cleanup must be idempotent and run ONLY on full find-omissions success (never after Step 1 alone — Q2); the manifest-existence check must be its own script, NOT embedded in validate-graph-arg.js (Q1 — that script's name/purpose stays narrow); ROLLBACK-*.json is removed at the same timing as the manifest (Q3 — a stale rollback would desync markers from the created tickets); cwd-relative manifest file paths (PX-137) are preserved; all messages are English, self-contained, and Action-directive.

acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: with a CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json present, require-consolidated-manifest.js exits 0; find-omissions Step 1 is the manifest-driven pipe flow (review then commit); on full success clean-consolidation-artifacts.js removes the manifest + rollback + empty dir

Error case: with no manifest, require-consolidated-manifest.js exits 2 and prints “run /consolidate-stubs first (Steps 1-5), then re-run /find-omissions” to stderr; clean-consolidation-artifacts.js exits 0 (idempotent) when nothing to remove
Edge case: cleanup leaves non-artifact files in manifests/ untouched and keeps the dir when non-empty; C003 handoff test stays green; validate-graph-arg.js is untouched

**[Happy path] — the complete green run**: a fresh session runs /consolidate-stubs (Steps 1-5) → manifests/CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-<ts>.json + manifests/ROLLBACK-<ts>.json exist → /find-omissions pre-flight passes both `|| exit 2` gates → Step 1 pipes the latest manifest into batch-create-resolving-tickets.js (--no-write review prints {createdTickets, skipped, rewrittenMarkers, dryRun:true}, then the real commit creates one resolving ticket per (sourceKey, unit) group and rewrites every on-disk marker key) → the residual preflight-stub-cleanup.js run reports no new classes → the inspection/merge/rename steps complete → the final step runs clean-consolidation-artifacts.js → manifests/ is gone and the tree is clean

**[Error case] — the missing-prerequisite abort**: a fresh session runs /find-omissions without first consolidating (or after a successful run removed the manifest) → require-consolidated-manifest.js prints a `[find-omissions] BLOCKED:` stderr line with the cause (no CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST-*.json) and the action (run /consolidate-stubs first Steps 1-5, then re-run /find-omissions) → exits 2 → the doc flow stops (`|| exit 2`) and zero tickets are created

**[Edge case] — idempotent hygiene**: clean-consolidation-artifacts.js run twice — the first removes the artifacts + empty dir, the second (nothing to remove) exits 0 with no output; a manifests/ containing unrelated.json keeps the file and the dir; a file named CONSOLIDATED-MANIFEST.json (no timestamp) or ROLLBACK.json is not touched; the find-omissions handoff note and consolidate-stubs.md L157 sentence still match the consume-and-remove story and print-manifest C003 stays green

tickets.background:
- **Goal**: enumerate-ticket-targets.js must stop emitting ORPHAN_TICKET_REF crimes for [::STUB::] text that lives inside quoted string literals or under test-fixture storage directories, so /make-ticket Step 8a no longer forces per-run classification of test data as false positives.
- **Purpose**: eliminate the recurring false-positive crime set (58 entries across tickets 129-138, every one marked false_positive) that pollutes Tickets.json targetCrimes, Malfeasance.json, and the spec Crimes section on every make run.
- **Motivation**: PX-90 eliminated the self-referential cascade (Tickets.json / Malfeasance.json) via file-name exclusion, but the test-fixture false-positive class was never addressed. enumerate-ticket-targets.js (PX-77) walks the whole repo with --dir=. and its scanFile is a line-based text match (line.includes('[::STUB::]') + extractTicketRef). It does not distinguish a real comment marker from marker text inside a quoted string literal or a fixture source file. Observed: the PX-138 make produced 7 ORPHAN_TICKET_REF crimes — 6 inside .test.cjs string literals (TS-001/002/003/004/006/007) and 1 inside tests/fixtures/src/p3.rs (TS-005). The existing review/find-all-stubs.js already ships the quoted-string rejection heuristic (STUB_IN_QUOTES_RE) and a fixtures-dir skip; enumerate lacks both, so the two scanners disagree.
- **Constraints**: TDD Red-Green-Refactor mandatory (Supreme Law §1); the primary fix is the scan algorithm (quoted-string rejection) — NOT a blanket tests/ exclusion; the fixtures-directory skip is an EXCEPTIONAL implementation covering only the test-fixture storage directory name, matching the existing find-all-stubs.js convention; the quoted-string heuristic is single-sourced in a shared lib so both scanners use the same detection; real marker detection (incl. tickets.title: find-omissions: exclude PX phase (phaseId=-1) tickets from inspection queue, tmp-omissions, and R<round> marking
tickets.background:
Goal: Exclude PX phase tickets (phaseId = -1) from the entire find-omissions pipeline so the PX backlog is never re-inspected, re-queued into _tmp files, or rewritten to R<round> status.

Purpose: The PX phase ("[X] Independent Phase", phaseId=-1) holds backlog tickets (140 in tools/conver) that are not part of the phased make->plan->start->review lifecycle. /find-omissions currently inspects ALL reviewed/remanded tickets across all phases, so the PX backlog dominates the inspection queue (140 of 177 candidates in the current tools/conver Tickets.json) and gets consumed by round-marking, diverging from the user decision that PX is out of scope.

Motivation: Audit of get-next-check-target-ticket.js (via create-check-target-tickets-cmds.js / create-tmp-omissions.js) and phasify-omissions.js found PX tickets processed in 4 code paths: (A1) collectReviewedTicketKeys queues PX reviewed/remanded tickets; (A2) collectNonReviewedTickets queues PX non-reviewed tickets; (A3) STUB-derived PX keys pass mergeTicketSources unfiltered; (A4) markPreMergeTicketsReviewed rewrites every pre-merge PX ticket to R<round>. User decision: PX is out of scope everywhere in find-omissions.

Constraints: PX phase id is -1; detection via phase.id === -1 or ticket.phaseId === -1 (verified 0 mismatches in current Tickets.json). All 3 project roots (root, tools/conver, crates/siprs) carry byte-identical copies of the affected scripts (md5 verified) — identical changes must be applied to every copy. R<round> is written only by phasify-omissions; after exclusion PX tickets keep their existing status (reviewed/remanded). PX-1 remanded in tools/conver is normalized to reviewed by the user outside this ticket. STUB-derived PX keys must be filtered too (A3). add-omission-ticket.js appendFoundOmissions continues to stage NEW omission clones in the tmp-omissions PX phase — that is new work, not the PX backlog, and phasify re-phases it out; kept as-is.

### Goal
Every find-omissions artifact (inspection queue, _tmp-omissions, round-marking) is free of PX backlog tickets, so the omission loop converges on the phased P0-P22 work only.

### Purpose
The PX phase is the independent backlog. Inspecting/round-marking it is semantically wrong: PX tickets are not part of the phase-ordered lifecycle and their inclusion makes the queue diverge. Excluding PX makes /find-omissions inspect exactly the phased work that can be re-implemented.

### Motivation
The audit (this ticket Background) demonstrated PX is processed in 4 places. The PX backlog (140 tickets) currently constitutes ~79% of the inspection queue, churning the loop without convergence benefit. The user explicitly decided PX is out of scope.

### Constraints
- phaseId detection: effective = ticket.phaseId !== undefined ? ticket.phaseId : phase.id; PX when === -1 (0 mismatches verified).
- 3 roots (root, tools/conver, crates/siprs) must receive byte-identical changes (md5 verified identical today).
- R<round> remains exclusive to phasify-omissions; exclusion leaves PX at reviewed/remanded.
- tickets.ts loadPendingTickets/checkAllReviewed are unchanged (PX stays reviewed = processed).
- add-omission-ticket staging in tmp-omissions PX phase is NEW work staging, not the backlog; kept.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Eliminate the 4 manual-bypass incidents in the /find-omissions pipeline so the pipeline runs unattended from Step 1 through Step 11.

### Purpose
Each script must refuse to create an invalid state, and when an invalid state is detected it must fail loudly (exit non-zero) instead of silently corrupting downstream artifacts.

### Motivation
Real runs forced manual intervention: (1) resolving tickets inherited foundOmissions/originalTicketKey/sentinel and were misclassified, (2) phasify silently skipped marker rewrite because stubs lost the line key, (3) tmp-omissions findings fragmented across two files, (4) add-omission-ticket created duplicate clones for the same key. Each bypass required a human to repair state by hand.

### Constraints
Edit only tools/conver/.claude; crates/siprs/.claude must remain byte-identical; successful-path behavior must not change; every fix follows TDD Red-Green-Refactor; run-all.js must converge to exactly the 14 pre-existing environmental failures.
